# MoonlightWeb

> MoonlightWeb is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0), self-hosted game-streaming server.
> Installed on the gaming PC, it captures and encodes that machine itself and serves
> it to any device with a web browser. It is also a full GameStream client, so
> Sunshine, Wolf and MultiSeat hosts on the network can be paired and streamed from
> the same page. Nothing to install on the client — just a URL.

## What it does

- Streams the gaming PC it runs on to any browser: phone, tablet, laptop, TV.
  No second streaming server: its own capture and encode engine handles Windows,
  Linux and macOS (DXGI/WGC, KMS/ScreenCast portal, ScreenCaptureKit; NVENC, AMF,
  Quick Sync, VA-API, VideoToolbox, with a software fallback stage).
- Up to 4K HDR at up to 240 fps, with H264, HEVC and AV1 codecs (hardware-decoded
  via WebCodecs).
- Under 20 ms latency over Wi-Fi using a WebRTC UDP transport with automatic
  fallback (UDP → TCP).
- GPU Video Enhancement in the browser (WebGPU running SGSRv1 + FSR1): stream at
  720p, display near-1440p quality.
- Full input support: keyboard, pointer-lock mouse, multi-touch trackpad, virtual
  keyboard, Xbox and PlayStation controllers with rumble.
- Zero-config: the machine it runs on needs no pairing at all (one card per
  display); other hosts — Sunshine/Apollo, Wolf (Games-on-Whales), MultiSeat — are
  auto-discovered on the LAN via mDNS and paired with a PIN.
- Internet access (opt-in): direct peer-to-peer WebRTC streams; per-session
  UPnP port mapping; no public DNS record or certificate. The host holds one
  outgoing connection to an introduction server and is reached at a link of its
  own; both ends ask a self-hosted STUN server for their public address.
  Pre-existing sub-domains keep working until February 2027.

## How it works

A small C++/Qt server runs on the gaming PC. It captures a GPU surface and hands it
straight to the GPU encoder inside the process that holds the WebRTC connection —
no loopback network hop, no RTP, no FEC — then sends video, audio and input to
browsers over WebRTC. For a host you pair with instead, the same server embeds
moonlight-common-c and speaks the GameStream protocol (RTSP/RTP/ENet) to it. The
client is 100% web: WebCodecs for decoding, WebGPU for rendering, AudioWorklet for
Opus audio.

## Platforms (server)

- Windows x64 / arm64 (guided .exe installer)
- macOS Apple Silicon (.pkg installer, or `brew install --cask linckosz/tap/moonlightweb`)
- Linux x64 (.deb, .rpm, portable AppImage, or the signed apt/dnf repositories
  and the AUR package `moonlightweb-bin`)

One command installs the right one on macOS and Linux, repository included:
`curl -fsSL https://moonlightweb.top/install.sh | bash`

The client requires no install: any modern browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox).
